## imaging

- [Data Preparation: Image](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/data.py): The image is the image of your galaxy, which comes from a telescope like the Hubble Space telescope (HST).
  - Contents: Pixel Scale, Loading Data From Individual Fits Files, Converting Data To Electrons Per Second, Resizing Data, Background Subtraction
- [Data Preparation: Noise-map](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/noise_map.py): The noise-map defines the uncertainty in every pixel of your lens image, where values are defined as the RMS standard deviation in every pixel (not the variances, HST WHT-map values, etc.).
  - Contents: Pixel Scale, Loading Data From Individual Fits Files, 1) Tools Illustrated In Image, Noise Conversions
- [Data Preparation: Extra Galaxies (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/extra_galaxies_centres.py): There may be extra galaxies nearby the lens and source galaxies, whose emission blends with the lens and source and whose mass may contribute to the ray-tracing and lens model.
  - Contents: Masking Extra Galaxies, Output
- [Data Preparation: Info (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/info.py): Auxiliary information about a strong lens dataset may used during an analysis or afterwards when interpreting the modeling results. For example, the redshifts of the source and lens galaxy.
- [Data Preparation: Lens Light Centre (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/lens_light_centre.py): This script marks the (y,x) arcsecond locations of the lens galaxy light centre(s) of the strong lens you are analysing. These can be used as fixed values for the lens light and mass models in a model-fit.
- [Data Preparation: Mask (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/mask.py): The mask removes the regions of the image where the lens and source galaxy are not present, typically the edges of the image.
- [Data Preparation: Extra Galaxies Mask (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/mask_extra_galaxies.py): There may be regions of an image that have signal near the lens and source that is from other galaxies not associated with the strong lens we are studying. The emission from these images will impact our model fitting and needs to be removed from the analysis.
  - Contents: Output
- [Data Preparation: Positions (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/optional/positions.py): The script manually marks the (y,x) arc-second positions of the multiply imaged lensed source galaxy in the image-plane, under the assumption that they originate from the same location in the source-plane.
- [Data Preparation: PSF](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/psf.py): The Point Spread Function (PSF) describes blurring due the optics of your dataset`s telescope. It is used by PyAutoLens when fitting a dataset to include these effects, such that does not bias the model.
  - Contents: Pixel Scale, Loading Data From Individual Fits Files, PSF Dimensions, PSF Normalization
- [GUI Preprocessing: Extra Galaxies Centres](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/extra_galaxies_centres.py): There may be extra galaxies nearby the lens and source galaxies, whose emission blends with the lens and source and whose mass may contribute to the ray-tracing and lens model.
  - Contents: Dataset, Search Box, Clicker, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Lens Light Centre](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/lens_light_centre.py): This tool allows one to input the lens light centre(s) of a strong lens(es) via a GUI, which can be used as a fixed value in pipelines.
  - Contents: Dataset, Search Box, Clicker, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Mask](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/mask.py): This tool allows one to mask a bespoke mask for a given image of a strong lens using an interactive GUI. This mask can then be loaded before a pipeline is run and passed to that pipeline so as to become the default masked used by a search (if a mask function is not passed to that search).
  - Contents: Dataset, Scribbler, Refining An Existing Mask, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Arc Mask (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/mask_arcs.py): This tool paints the lensed ARCS and multiple images of the source, and keeps only those: everything you do not paint, lens light included, is masked. The product isolates the source, which is what a source-only fit, an arc signal-to-noise measurement or a source-plane analysis should look at.
  - Contents: Dataset, Scribbler, Refining An Existing Mask, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Extra Galaxies Mask (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/mask_extra_galaxies.py): There may be regions of an image that have signal near the lens and source that is from other galaxies not associated with the strong lenswe are studying. The emission from these images will impact our model fitting and needs to be removed from the analysis.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Scribbler, Refining An Existing Mask, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Extra Galaxies Mask, Multi-Wavelength (Optional)](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/mask_extra_galaxies_multi.py): A multi-wavelength dataset needs one extra galaxies mask per waveband: what should be masked is not the same in every filter (a contaminant can be bright in one and absent in another), and the wavebands are often on different pixel grids, so a mask cannot simply be copied across.
  - Contents: Dataset, First Waveband, Next Waveband, Output
- [GUI Preprocessing: Positions](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/gui/positions.py): This tool allows one to input the positions of strong lenses via a GUI, which can be used to penalize inaccurate mass models during lensing modeling.
  - Contents: Dataset, Search Box, Clicker, Output
- [Manual Preprocessing: Mask Irregular](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/manual/mask_irregular.py): (no summary in script docstring)
- [Imaging: Data Preparation](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/start_here.py): When a CCD imaging dataset is analysed, it must conform to certain standards in order for the analysis to be performed correctly. This tutorial describes these standards and links to more detailed scripts which will help you prepare your dataset to adhere to them if it does not already.
  - Contents: Pixel Scale, Image, Noise Map, PSF, Data Processing Complete

Modelling their light helps us separate the two and infer the properties of the lens and source.

- [Features: Pixelization](scripts/imaging/features/pixelization/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lensing stretches a background galaxy into arcs and multiple images. A pixelized source reconstruction uses those observations, together with a lens mass model, to infer what the galaxy looks like before lensing. It is particularly useful when the source has spiral arms, star-forming clumps or irregular structure that a simple smooth light profile struggles to describe.

- [Features: Scaling Relation](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/start_here.py): A scaling relation connects the properties of a galaxy population through a shared rule, rather than giving every member a completely independent model. In these lensing examples, member luminosities help determine their mass normalizations.
- [Simulator: Manual Signal to Noise Ratio](scripts/imaging/features/simulator_manual_signal_to_noise_ratio.py): When simulating `Imaging` of a strong lens, one is often not concerned with the actual units of the light (e.g. electrons per second, counts, etc.) but instead simple wants the data to correspond to a certain signal to noise value.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Simulate, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json
- [Fits](scripts/imaging/fit.py): This guide shows how to fit data using the `FitImaging` object, including visualizing and interpreting its results.
  - Contents: Loading Data, Mask, Fitting, Bad Fit, Fit Quantities, Figures of Merit, Plane Quantities, Unmasked Quantities, Pixel Counting, Outputting Results
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Inversion (Parametric)__](scripts/imaging/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Imaging` data with a lens light profile and source light profile (e.g. an elliptical Sersic lens and source).
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Lens Galaxy Mass, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Light Profile, Lens Light, Ray Tracing, Source Image, Convolution, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Imaging: Modeling](scripts/imaging/modeling.py): This script is the starting point for lens modeling of CCD imaging data (E.g. Hubble Space Telescope, Euclid) with **PyAutoLens** and it provides an overview of the lens modeling API.
  - Contents: Model, Plotters, Simulation, Data Preparation, Dataset & Mask, Extra Galaxies Noise Scaling, Over Sampling, Model Composition, Coordinates, Improved Lens Model, Linear Light Profiles, Concise API, Search, Unique Identifier, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Features, HowToLens, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Imaging](scripts/imaging/plot.py): This example shows how to plot an `Imaging` dataset and a `FitImaging` fit, figure by figure and via multi-panel subplots.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Plane Images, Plane Subplots, Fit Subplot, Fit Subplot (Log10), Tracer Subplot, Outputting to FITS, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Start Here](scripts/imaging/simulator.py): This script is the starting point for simulating galaxy-galaxy strong lenses as CCD imaging data (E.g. Hubble Space Telescope, Euclid) and it provides an overview of the lens simulation API.
  - Contents: Model, Plotters, Dataset Paths, Grid, Over Sampling, PSF Convolution, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json, Multiple Images, JAX Variant (Advanced), Oversampled PSF (Advanced)
- [Simulator: Sample](scripts/imaging/simulator_sample.py): This script illustrates how to simulate a sample of `Imaging` datasets of 'galaxy-scale' strong lenses, which can easily be used to simulate hundreds or thousands of strong lenses.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Simulate, Sample Model Distributions, Sample Instances
- [Source Science](scripts/imaging/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Simulated Dataset, Mask, Source Values, Source Flux, Source Magnification, Tracer, Magnification At A Point, Magnification Map, Source-Plane Magnification Map, Area Magnification, Parametric Source Models, Magnification Errors, Magnification Uncertainty Map
- [Start Here: Imaging](scripts/imaging/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses are often observed with CCD imaging, for example using HST, JWST, or ground-based telescopes.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Extra Galaxy Removal, Masking, Model, Model Fit, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Result, Extra Galaxy Removal GUI, Model Your Own Lens, Simulator, Sample, Wrap Up

Their light is traced through the relevant sequence of planes to predict the observed image.

- [Features: Mass Stellar Dark](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/start_here.py): A decomposed mass model separates the mass associated with stellar light from a dark-halo contribution. It provides an alternative to describing the total mass with a single profile.

- [Features: Operated Light Profile](scripts/group/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/start_here.py): An operated light profile describes emission after an instrumental operation has already been included in the profile. For imaging, the common example is a profile that already describes the PSF-blurred appearance of compact emission.

- [Features: Shapelets](scripts/group/features/advanced/shapelets/start_here.py): Shapelets describe light as a weighted combination of basis functions. Unlike a single smooth light profile, the basis contains functions with different spatial structures, allowing their sum to describe more complicated galaxy morphology.

- [Features: Sky Background](scripts/group/features/advanced/sky_background/start_here.py): The background contributes light across an image in addition to the galaxy or lens being studied. If a background contribution remains in the data, it can be included in the model rather than attributed to the target's emission.
- [Subhalo Detection: Group](scripts/group/features/advanced/subhalo/detect/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses can be used to detect the presence of small-scale dark matter (DM) subhalos. This occurs when the DM subhalo overlaps the lensed source emission, and therefore gravitationally perturbs the observed image of the lensed source galaxy.
  - Contents: SLaM Pipelines, Grid Search, Group Adaptation, Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, SLaM Pipeline Functions, Bayesian Evidence, Grid Search Result

- [Features: Subhalo](scripts/group/features/advanced/subhalo/start_here.py): A dark matter subhalo can perturb lensed emission without supplying visible light of its own. The effect depends on the halo properties, its location relative to the arcs and the larger lens model.

- [Features: Group Halo](scripts/group/features/group_halo/start_here.py): A group-scale lens may be described by the mass of its individual galaxies, by those galaxies plus a shared group halo, or by other suitable mass components. A shared halo is a modelling choice rather than a requirement imposed by the name “group”.

- [Features: Linear Light Profiles](scripts/group/features/linear_light_profiles/start_here.py): A linear light profile has the same spatial form as an ordinary light profile, but its intensity is solved during each likelihood evaluation instead of being sampled by the non-linear search.

Each Gaussian describes emission on a particular spatial scale; together, they can provide a flexible model of the galaxy.

- [Features: Scaling Relation](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/start_here.py): A scaling relation connects the properties of a galaxy population through a shared rule, rather than giving every member a completely independent model. In these lensing examples, member luminosities help determine their mass normalizations.
- [Fits: Group](scripts/group/fit.py): This guide shows how to fit data using the `FitImaging` object for group-scale strong lenses, including visualizing and interpreting its results.
  - Contents: Loading Data, Mask, Galaxy Centres, Fitting, Bad Fit, Fit Quantities, Figures of Merit, Plane Quantities, Unmasked Quantities, Pixel Counting, Outputting Results, Over Sampling
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Group__](scripts/group/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Imaging` data of a group-scale strong lens, where there are multiple lens galaxies whose mass profiles all contribute to the ray-tracing of the source galaxy.
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Main Lens Galaxy, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy Light Profile, Lens Light, Lens Galaxy Mass, Ray Tracing, Source Image, Convolution, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Group: Modeling](scripts/group/modeling.py): This script models an example strong lens on the 'group' scale, which typically have one or more "main" lens galaxies and smaller extra galaxies nearby, whose light may blur with the source light and whose mass contributes significantly to the ray-tracing, meaning both are therefore included in the strong lens model.
  - Contents: Scaling Relations, Group Halo, Example, Simulation, Data Preparation, Dataset & Mask, Main Galaxies and Extra Galaxies, Centres, Redshifts, Model, Coordinates, Improved Lens Model, Linear Light Profiles, Over Sampling, Search, Unique Identifier, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Features, HowToLens, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Group](scripts/group/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a group-scale `Imaging` dataset and a `FitImaging` fit, figure by figure and via multi-panel subplots.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Plane Images, Fit Subplot, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Group](scripts/group/simulator.py): This script simulates an example strong lens on the 'group' scale, where there is a single primary lens galaxy and two smaller extra galaxies nearby, whose mass contributes significantly to the ray-tracing and is therefore included in the strong lens model.
  - Contents: Main Lens Galaxies vs Extra Galaxies, No Group Halo, Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, PSF Convolution, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Visualize, Tracer json, Centre JSON Files
- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): Group Scale](scripts/group/slam.py): This script uses the SLaM pipelines to fit a group-scale strong lens, including extra galaxies and scaling galaxies surrounding the main lens whose light and mass are both modeled.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Extra Galaxies and Scaling Galaxies, This Script, SOURCE LP PIPELINE 0, SOURCE LP PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, LIGHT LP PIPELINE, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Dataset, Galaxy Centres, Mask, Settings AutoFit, SLaM Pipeline
- [Source Science: Group](scripts/group/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Simulated Dataset, Mask, Source Values, Source Flux, Source Magnification, Impact of Extra Galaxies, Tracer, Magnification At A Point, Area Magnification, Parametric Source Models, Magnification Errors, Magnification Uncertainty Map
- [Start Here: Group](scripts/group/start_here.py): Group scale lenses typically have multiple lens galaxies whose light and mass all contribute significantly to the lensing of the source galaxy. Groups typically also have just one lensed source.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Main Lens Galaxies, Masking, Model, Model Fit, Live Visual Update, Result, Centre Input GUI, Model Your Own Lens, Wrap Up

## interferometer

- [Interferometer: CASA Reduction](scripts/interferometer/casa_reduction.py): This script is a practical walkthrough of how to reduce an ALMA / JVLA interferometer observation with **CASA** and export it into the three FITS files that **PyAutoLens** expects for lens modeling:
  - Contents: PyAutoLens Requirements, CASA in Five Steps, Step 1 — Split by Field / SPW, Step 2 — Channel Averaging, Step 3 — Continuum Subtraction, Step 4 — Rescale Sigmas, Step 5 — Export to FITS, Combining Spectral Windows, Polarisations, Building the Interferometer Object, Troubleshooting, SLACK
- [Interferometer: Data Preparation](scripts/interferometer/data_preparation.py): When an interferometer dataset is analysed, it must conform to certain standards in order for the analysis to be performed correctly. This tutorial describes these standards and links to more detailed scripts which will help you prepare your dataset to adhere to them if it does not already.
  - Contents: SLACK, Pixel Scale, Visibilities, Noise-Map, UV Wavelengths, Real Space Mask, Data Processing Complete, Positions (Optional), Lens Light Centre (Optional), Extra Galaxies (Optional), Mask Extra Galaxies (Optional), Info (Optional)
- [Modeling Features: Operated Light Profiles (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/modeling.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Model, Search, Analysis, Run Time, Model-Fit, Result
- [Simulator: Light Operated (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/simulator.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, uv-wavelengths, Simulator, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json
- [Features: Operated Light Profile](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/start_here.py): An operated light profile describes emission after an instrumental operation has already been included in the profile. For imaging, the common example is a profile that already describes the PSF-blurred appearance of compact emission.
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Potential Correction (Interferometer)__](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/potential_correction/likelihood_function.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/advanced/potential_correction/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Simplifications, Prerequisites, Dataset, Source Inversion Blocks, Dpsi Mesh, Correction Response, Joint Response, Dense Route, Sparse (w-tilde) Route, Solve, Dkappa Map, Evidence Terms, Verification, JAX / xp, Wrap Up
- [Feature: Potential Correction (Gravitational Imaging)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/potential_correction/start_here.py): This example performs gravitational imaging on interferometer data: pixelized corrections $\delta\psi$ to the lensing potential are reconstructed jointly with the pixelized source, revealing mass structure (e.g. dark subhaloes) the smooth lens model omits, as a convergence-correction map $\delta\kappa = \frac{1}{2}\nabla^2\delta\psi$.
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets Fit (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/fit.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Negative Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Basis, Fit, Intensities, Visualization, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/modeling.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, NUFFT (nufftax), Positive Negative Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Over Sampling, Search, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Wrap Up
- [Features: Shapelets](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/start_here.py): Shapelets describe light as a weighted combination of basis functions. Unlike a single smooth light profile, the basis contains functions with different spatial structures, allowing their sum to describe more complicated galaxy morphology.
- [Subhalo Detection: Start Here](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/detect/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses can be used to detect the presence of small-scale dark matter (DM) subhalos. This occurs when the DM subhalo overlaps the lensed source emission, and therefore gravitationally perturbs the observed image of the lensed source galaxy.
  - Contents: SLaM Pipelines, Grid Search, Pixelized Source, Model, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Two Datasets, Sparse Operators, Settings, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, SLaM Pipeline
- [Sensitivity](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/sensitivity/start_here.py): Sensitivity mapping tests how an analysis responds to injected subhalos. It repeats a controlled recovery experiment across positions or other halo properties to characterize which signals the chosen setup can distinguish.
- ["](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/simulator.py): Simulator: Subhalo ==================
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Simulate, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json
- [Features: Subhalo](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/start_here.py): A dark matter subhalo can perturb lensed emission without supplying visible light of its own. The effect depends on the halo properties, its location relative to the arcs and the larger lens model.

- [Start Here: Datacube](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/start_here.py): A datacube is a stack of interferometer observations of the same lens taken across many spectral channels — for example, an ALMA observation of a CO emission line in a high-redshift lensed galaxy, where each channel records visibilities at a slightly different frequency. The lens galaxy is the same in every channel, but the source's emission-line morphology varies across the cube: bright in channels close to the line peak, faint in channels at the line wings, and shifting in shape if the source has internal velocity structure.
  - Contents: JAX, Imports, Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Dataset Loading, Sparse Operators, Positions, Settings, Mesh Shape, Model, Per-Channel Analyses, FactorGraph, Search, Model Fit, Result, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Extra Galaxies](scripts/interferometer/features/extra_galaxies/modeling.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/interferometer/features/extra_galaxies/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.

- [Features: Scaling Relation](scripts/point_source/features/scaling_relation/start_here.py): A scaling relation connects the properties of a galaxy population through a shared rule, rather than giving every member a completely independent model. In these lensing examples, member luminosities help determine their mass normalizations.
- [Modeling: Time Delays](scripts/point_source/features/time_delays.py): A measurable quantity of a point source is its time delay—the time it takes for light to travel from the source to the observer for each multiple image of the point source (e.g., the quasar images). This is often expressed as the relative time delay between each image and the image with the shortest time delay, which is often referred to as the "reference image."
  - Contents: Model, Dataset, Point Solver, Search, Analysis, Run Times, Result, Cosmology

  - Contents: Lensed Point Source, Point Source, Point Solver, Number of Solutions, Solving the Lens Equation, Triangle Tracing, Dataset, Name Pairing, Fitting, Magnification At The Multiple Images, Chi Squared, Solved Source Centre, Fluxes, Flux Point Dataset, Flux Fitting, Time Delays, Time Delay Fitting, New User Wrap Up, Shape Solver
- [Modeling: Start Here](scripts/point_source/modeling.py): This script is the starting point for lens modeling of point-source lens datasets, for example the multiple image positions of a lensed quasar.
  - Contents: Not Using Light Profiles, Model, Dataset, Point Solver, Model Composition, Name Pairing, Coordinates, Search, Unique Identifier, Live Visual Update, Chi Squared, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Results, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Point Source](scripts/point_source/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a `PointDataset` and a `FitPointDataset` fit.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Start Here](scripts/point_source/simulator.py): This script is the starting point for simulating point source strong lens datasets, for example a lensed quasar or supernova, and it provides an overview of the lens simulation API.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Ray Tracing, Point Solver, Point Datasets, Visualize, Tracer json, Imaging, Point Source Images, Fluxes, Point Dataset, Time Delays, JAX Variant (Advanced)
- [Simulator: Hubble Constant Time Delays](scripts/point_source/simulator_sample.py): A multiply imaged lensed quasar with time delays can measure the Hubble constant, which is a fundamental Cosmological parameter that describes the rate of expansion of the universe. This is because the the difference between the geometric time delay and the physical time delay is proportional to the Hubble constant.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Point Solver, Sample Model Distributions, Simulate, Sample Instances
- [Start Here: Point Source](scripts/point_source/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses often have point sources (e.g. quasars) that are being lensed, appearing as two or four distinct point-like images. These lenses are particularly useful for measuring cosmological parameters like the Hubble constant, and for studying the small-scale properties of dark matter.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Point Solver, Model, Name Pairing, Model Fit, Live Visual Update, Result, Model Your Own Lens, Fluxes and Time Delays, Simulator, Sample, Wrap Up

## cluster

- [CSV API: Cluster](scripts/cluster/csv_api.py): Cluster lens modelling uses a small family of CSV files as its canonical input format. Rather than composing a tracer and a model inline in Python, the cluster workflow stores every component — main galaxies, dark-matter halo, source light, source point components, scaling-tier members — in spreadsheet-editable CSVs that are then loaded into PyAutoLens objects.
  - Contents: Imports & Output Path, Point Dataset CSV, Galaxy Model CSV API, Scaling Galaxies CSV, af.Model[Galaxy] from CSVs, Wrap Up
- [Lenstool Users: Data Preparation (SMACS J0723)](scripts/cluster/lenstool/data.py): This script prepares everything needed to repeat a *published Lenstool cluster analysis* in **PyAutoLens**: the strong-lensing model of the first JWST cluster, SMACS J0723.3-7327, by Mahler et al. 2023 (ApJ 945, 49; arXiv:2207.07101).
  - Contents: Paths + URLs, Downloads, Coordinate Convention, Parse arcs.dat, Parse galcat.cat, Parse best.par, Image Cutout, Write CSVs
- [Lenstool Users: Cluster Modeling (SMACS J0723)](scripts/cluster/lenstool/modeling.py): **If you model galaxy clusters with Lenstool, this script is for you.** It repeats a published Lenstool analysis — Mahler et al. 2023's model of SMACS J0723, the first JWST cluster — in **PyAutoLens**, in three steps:
  - Contents: Load Data, The Published Model, Reconstructed, Verification I — source-plane compactness, Verification II — image-plane RMS (optional), Critical Curves (optional), The Refit
- [Lenstool Users: dPIE Parameterization Mapping (Scaling Galaxies)](scripts/cluster/lenstool/parameterization_mapping.py): **If you want to fit cluster member (scaling) galaxies without knowing the source or lens redshift, this script shows you how — and proves it recovers the standard Lenstool model exactly once the redshifts become known.**
- [Log Likelihood Function: Cluster Point Source](scripts/cluster/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the cluster point-source ``log_likelihood_function``, the figure-of-merit Nautilus optimises when fitting a cluster lens model to ``point_datasets.csv``.
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset, Truth Model, Tracer, Source-Plane Chi Squared: Concept, Multi-Plane Ray Tracing, Back-Traced Source-Plane Positions, Source-Plane Centroid, Residual Map, Lensing Jacobian at Positions, Chi Squared Map (Source), Per-Source Chi Squared, Total Chi Squared (Source), Noise Normalization (Source), Source-Plane Log Likelihood, Source-Plane Validation, Opt-In Magnification Weighting, Image-Plane Chi Squared: Concept, Point Solver Setup, Forward Solving Model Positions, Pairing Model to Observed, Image-Plane Residual Map, Chi Squared Map (Image), Per-Source / Total Chi Squared, Noise Normalization (Image), Image-Plane Log Likelihood, Image-Plane Validation, Source-Plane vs Image-Plane: When to Use Which, Wrap Up
- [Cluster & Group Mass Parameterizations](scripts/cluster/mass_parameterizations.py): **A plain-language tour of the ways to parameterize and couple the masses in a Lenstool-style cluster model — the cluster-scale halo, the BCG and other individually-freed galaxies, and the member ("scaling") population.**
  - Contents: Model 1 — The Standard Lenstool Model, Model 2 — The Angular (b0) Parameterization, Model 3 — Mass Anchoring, Model 4 — The Two-Parameter Relation
- [Mass Parameterizations II — Mapping Lenstool onto PyAutoLens](scripts/cluster/mass_parameterizations_pyautolens.py): **For Lenstool users: how and why PyAutoLens re-expresses the standard Lenstool cluster / group model in its native parameterization for multi-galaxy lenses (MGLs), with the scaling galaxies keeping the dPIE's truncation throughout.**
- [Modeling: Cluster](scripts/cluster/modeling.py): This script models the small multi-plane cluster lens simulated by ``cluster/simulator.py``: a Brightest Cluster Galaxy (BCG) plus one satellite member at the lens redshift ``z = 0.5``, 10 lower-mass cluster members modelled collectively via a luminosity-mass scaling relation, a standalone NFW host dark matter halo *not* tied to any individual galaxy, and 2 background sources at *different* redshifts (``z = 1.0`` and ``z = 2.0``) which the cluster lenses into multiple images.
  - Contents: Example, Simulation, Dataset, Model CSVs, Scaling Galaxies Table, Point Solver, Chi Squared, Cluster Components, Redshifts, Model, Scaling Relation, Name Pairing, Search, Live Visual Update, Analysis, Factor Graph, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result
- [Plots: Cluster](scripts/cluster/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a cluster-scale strong lens dataset — the multiple-image positions of its lensed sources, individually and overlaid together on an image of the cluster.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Positions Overlay, Image Group Zooms, Cluster Subplot, Tracer, Critical Curves, Caustics, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Cluster](scripts/cluster/simulator.py): This script simulates an example strong lens on the 'cluster' scale: a small cluster consisting of 2 main lens galaxies (a brightest cluster galaxy + a single satellite), 10 lower-mass cluster member galaxies on a luminosity-mass scaling relation, a single host dark matter halo not tied to any individual galaxy, and 2 multiply-imaged background source galaxies sitting at *different* redshifts (``z = 1.0`` and ``z = 2.0``) — making this a genuine multi-plane lens.
  - Contents: Multi-Plane Setup, Main Lens vs Scaling Members vs Host Halo vs Source Galaxies, Dataset Paths, Imaging and Visualization Grids, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Scaling Member Galaxies, Host Dark Matter Halo, Source Galaxies, Ray Tracing, JAX JIT, Point Solver, Point Datasets, Combined CSV, Manual CSV Editing, Scaling Galaxies CSV, Model CSVs, Tracer JSON, Imaging, Visualize
- [Start Here: Cluster](scripts/cluster/start_here.py): Cluster-scale strong lenses are made of:
  - Contents: JAX, Capabilities, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Model CSVs, Scaling Galaxies Table, Point Solver, Cluster Components, Model, Analysis + Factor Graph, Search, Model Fit, Live Visual Update, Result, Wrap Up

- [Features: Shapelets](scripts/multi_galaxy/features/advanced/shapelets/start_here.py): Shapelets describe light as a weighted combination of basis functions. Unlike a single smooth light profile, the basis contains functions with different spatial structures, allowing their sum to describe more complicated galaxy morphology.

- [Features: Sky Background](scripts/multi_galaxy/features/advanced/sky_background/start_here.py): The background contributes light across an image in addition to the galaxy or lens being studied. If a background contribution remains in the data, it can be included in the model rather than attributed to the target's emission.

- [Features: Subhalo](scripts/multi_galaxy/features/advanced/subhalo/start_here.py): A dark matter subhalo can perturb lensed emission without supplying visible light of its own. The effect depends on the halo properties, its location relative to the arcs and the larger lens model.

Each Gaussian describes emission on a particular spatial scale; together, they can provide a flexible model of the galaxy.

In these lensing examples, member luminosities help determine their mass normalizations.

  - Contents: Loading Data, Extra Galaxies Noise Scaling, Mask, Galaxies, Per-Galaxy Deflections, Fitting, Bad Fit, Fit Quantities, Figures of Merit, Plane Quantities, Per-Galaxy Quantities, Unmasked Quantities, Pixel Counting, Outputting Results
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Multi Galaxy (Parametric)__](scripts/multi_galaxy/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Imaging` data of a **multi-galaxy** strong lens, where two (or more) galaxies of comparable mass both contribute significantly to the lensing of a single background source.
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset, Extra Galaxies Noise Scaling, Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Main Lens Galaxy Light (Setup), Main Lens Galaxy Mass, Summed Deflection Field, Main Lens Galaxies, Source Galaxy Light Profile, Lens Light, Ray Tracing, Source Image, Convolution, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up

  - Contents: Example, Plotters, Simulation, Data Preparation, Dataset, Extra Galaxies Noise Scaling, Main Lens Galaxies, Mask, Over Sampling, Redshifts, Model, External Shear, Model Composition, Coordinates, Improved Lens Model, Linear Light Profiles, Concise API, Search, Unique Identifier, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Loading From Output Folder, Source Science (Magnification, Flux and More), Features, HowToLens, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Multi Galaxy](scripts/multi_galaxy/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a multi-galaxy `Imaging` dataset and a `FitImaging` fit, figure by figure and via multi-panel subplots.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Plane Images, Fit Subplot, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Multi Galaxy](scripts/multi_galaxy/simulator.py): This script simulates an example strong lens on the 'multi galaxy' scale, where two (or more) galaxies of comparable mass both contribute significantly to the lensing of a single background source. Neither galaxy is a minor perturber: they are **co-dominant deflectors**, and every one of them is modeled individually with its own free light and mass profiles.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Extra Galaxy Centre, Over Sampling, PSF Convolution, Main Lens Galaxies, External Shear, Source Galaxy, Extra Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Mask Extra Galaxies, Visualize, Tracer json, Centre JSON Files, Positions, JAX Variant
- [Simulator: Sample (Multi Galaxy)](scripts/multi_galaxy/simulator_sample.py): This script illustrates how to simulate a sample of `Imaging` datasets of 'multi-galaxy' strong lenses, which can easily be used to simulate hundreds or thousands of them.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Simulate, Sample Truth Distributions, Sample Instances
- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): Multi Galaxy](scripts/multi_galaxy/slam.py): This script is the multi-galaxy regime's SLaM pipeline: the production path for fitting a lens with two or more co-dominant deflectors, as opposed to the single-search fits of `multi_galaxy/modeling.py`.
  - Contents: Why A Regime Baseline Exists, What Changes, Source LP Pipeline, Source Pix Pipeline 1, Source Pix Pipeline 2, Light LP Pipeline, Mass Total Pipeline, Dataset, Centres, Mask & Over Sampling, SLaM Pipeline
- [Source Science: Multi Galaxy](scripts/multi_galaxy/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Simulated Dataset, Mask, Source Values, Source Flux, Source Magnification, Single Deflector Comparison, Tracer, Magnification At A Point, Area Magnification, Parametric Source Models, Magnification Errors, Magnification Uncertainty Map
- [Start Here: Multi Galaxy](scripts/multi_galaxy/start_here.py): Multi-galaxy strong lenses have **two or more galaxies of comparable mass which both contribute significantly to the lensing** of a single background source. Neither galaxy is a minor perturber — they are co-dominant deflectors, and every one of them gets its own free light and mass model.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Extra Galaxies, Main Lens Galaxies, Masking, Model, Model Fit, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Result, Extra Galaxies GUI, Model Your Own Lens, Simulator, Sample, Wrap Up

## weak

- [Real Data: Combined Strong + Weak Lensing of Abell 2744](scripts/weak/features/strong_lensing/a2744.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/weak/features/strong_lensing/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Dataset (Strong), Dataset (Weak), Model, Analysis Factors & Factor Graph, Search & Model-Fit, Result
- [Fit: Combined Strong + Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/features/strong_lensing/fit.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/weak/features/strong_lensing/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Dataset, Tracer, Imaging Fit, Weak Fit, Joint Likelihood, Shear Profile
- [Modeling: Combined Strong + Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/features/strong_lensing/modeling.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/weak/features/strong_lensing/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Dataset, Model, Analysis List, Analysis Factor & Factor Graph, Search & Model-Fit, Result
- [Simulator: Combined Strong + Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/features/strong_lensing/simulator.py): Read the [feature introduction](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/blob/main/notebooks/weak/features/strong_lensing/start_here.ipynb) for the shared concepts and a guide to the examples.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Ray Tracing, Imaging Simulation, Weak Simulation, Output
- [Features: Strong Lensing](scripts/weak/features/strong_lensing/start_here.py): Strong and weak lensing probe different parts of a mass distribution. A combined analysis connects central strongly lensed features with the wider weak-lensing field through a shared mass model.
- [Fit: Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/fit.py): This script shows how to fit a strong-lens mass model to a weak gravitational lensing shear catalogue. Where the `imaging` and `interferometer` workflows fit a 2D image of a lensed source, the weak-lensing workflow fits a set of (gamma_2, gamma_1) shear measurements at the (y, x) positions of background source galaxies — a ``WeakDataset`` produced by the simulator script in `scripts/weak/simulator.py`.
  - Contents: Dataset, Model, Fit, Visualization, Shear Profile, Notes
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Weak Lensing__](scripts/weak/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the **PyAutoLens** likelihood function for fitting a lens mass model to a weak gravitational lensing shear catalogue (a `WeakDataset`). It is the weak-lensing companion of the guides for the other dataset types (e.g. `scripts/imaging/likelihood_function.py`), following the same style and level of detail.
  - Contents: Dataset, Lens Galaxy, Shear Field Evaluation, Residuals, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Analysis, Wrap Up
- [Modeling: Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/modeling.py): This script fits a lens mass model to a weak gravitational lensing shear catalogue using a non-linear search. It is the weak-lensing analogue of `scripts/imaging/modeling.py`: where that script infers a lens model from a 2D image of a lensed source, this script infers one from the (gamma_2, gamma_1) shear measurements of background source galaxies — a `WeakDataset` produced by `scripts/weak/simulator.py`.
  - Contents: Dataset, Model, Search, Analysis, Run Times, Model-Fit, Output Folder Layout, Result
- [Plots: Weak](scripts/weak/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a `WeakDataset` and a `FitWeak` fit.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Convergence Map, Fit, Fit Figures, Fit Subplot, Shear Profile, Visualizer
- [Real Data: Weak Lensing of Abell 2744](scripts/weak/real_data/a2744.py): This script fits a dark-matter halo mass model to a **real weak-lensing shape catalogue** of the merging galaxy cluster Abell 2744 ("Pandora's Cluster", z = 0.308) — the first PyAutoLens weak-lensing analysis of real sky data, and the capstone of the weak-lensing example series.
  - Contents: Catalogue Download, Catalogue Load & Projection, Quality Cuts, Weak Dataset, Mass Map, Model & Search, Result
- [Simulator: Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/simulator.py): This script simulates a weak gravitational lensing shear catalogue. Unlike the imaging simulator (which produces a 2D image of the lensed source) the weak-lensing simulator produces a *catalogue* of (gamma_2, gamma_1) shear measurements at the (y, x) positions of a population of background source galaxies.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Ray Tracing, Source Positions, Simulator, Output, Visualize
- [Start Here: Weak Lensing](scripts/weak/start_here.py): Gravitational lensing does not stop at the spectacular arcs and multiple images of strong lensing. Every galaxy behind a massive structure is slightly sheared by its gravity — a percent-level distortion invisible in any single galaxy but measurable statistically across thousands. This is **weak lensing**, and it traces mass on scales far beyond the strong-lensing core.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Catalogue Download, Catalogue Load & Projection, Quality Cuts, Weak Dataset, Mass Map, Model, Model Fit, Result, Model Your Own Catalogue, Simulator, Wrap Up

## guides

- [Misc: Add A Profile](scripts/guides/advanced/add_a_profile.py): **PyAutoLens** supports a wide range of mass and light profiles for modelling the lens and source galaxies in strong gravitational lensing systems.
  - Contents: Source Code, Example Mass Profile, Inheritance Structure, Data Structure Decorators, Transform Decorator, Lens Modeling, Lens Modeling Configs, Deflections, Spherical Template, Physical Profiles, Light Profiles
- [Misc: Custom Analysis](scripts/guides/advanced/custom_analysis.py): Users familiar with **PyAutoLens** will have seen that `Analysis` classes are used to performed lens modeling of different datasets. For example, the `AnalysisImaging` class fits imaging datasets, the `AnalysisInterferometer` class fits interferometer datasets.
  - Contents: PyAutoFit, Source Code, Example Analysis Class, Lens Model, Instances, Simple Analysis Example, Analysis Class Considerations, Model Fit, Weak Lensing Example, Result, To Do List
- [Misc: Multi-Plane](scripts/guides/advanced/multi_plane.py): Multi-plane ray-tracing is used when a lens system has more planes than just an image-plane and source-plane. When tracing from one plane to the next, the redshifts of the planes are used to compute scaling factors that are applied to the deflection angles, so that every plane's lensing effect is combined consistently.
  - Contents: Example, Ray Tracing, Trace, Lensing Units vs Physical Units, The PyAutoLens Convention, Profiles With Physical Units, Science Corollaries, Cross Validation, Attribution
- [Over Sampling](scripts/guides/advanced/over_sampling.py): Throughout the workspace, we have created 2D grids of (y,x) coordinates and input them into light profiles to compute their image.
  - Contents: Illustration, Numerics, Images, Adaptive Over Sampling, Multiple Lens Galaxies, Ray Tracing, Default Ray Tracing, Dataset & Modeling, Pixelization
- [Chaining: Over Sample](scripts/guides/advanced/over_sampling_chaining.py): Over sampling is a numerical technique where the images of light profiles and galaxies are evaluated on a higher resolution grid than the image data to ensure the calculation is accurate.
  - Contents: Start Here Notebook, Dataset + Masking, Paths, Redshifts, Model (Search 1), Search + Analysis + Model-Fit (Search 1), Result (Search 1), Over Sampling (Search 2)
- [COOLEST](scripts/guides/coolest_interop.py): COOLEST (COde-independent Organized LEns STandard, https://github.com/aymgal/COOLEST) is a standard for storing and exchanging strong lens models between different lens modeling software, for example lenstronomy, herculens and GLEE.
  - Contents: Conventions, Lens Model, Export, Import, Round Trip, Mass Fields, NFW Profiles, Unsupported Profiles
- [Data Structures](scripts/guides/data_structures.py): This tutorial illustrates the data structure objects which data and results quantities are stored using, which are extensions of NumPy arrays.
  - Contents: JAX, Units, API, Grids, Native, Slim, Masked Data Structures, Data, Tracer, Irregular Structures, Vector Quantities
- [Galaxies](scripts/guides/galaxies.py): In the guide `tracer.py`, we inspected the results of a `Tracer` and computed the overall properties of the lens model's image, convergence and other quantities.
  - Contents: JAX, Units, Data Structures, Grids, Tracer, Individual Lens Galaxy Components, Log10
- [HPC: Example CPU and GPU](scripts/guides/hpc/example_cpu_and_gpu.py): This example illustrates how to set up lens modeling on a High Performance Computing (HPC) system, using either multiple CPUs or a GPU.
  - Contents: HPC Output Path, HPC Dataset Path, HPC Home Path, Batch Script: Many Datasets (Array Job), Dataset, Batch Script: Single Dataset with Multiple CPUs, Nautilus CPUs, Lens Modeling, GPU Jobs
- [Lens Calc](scripts/guides/lens_calc.py): This guide explains the ``LensCalc`` class, which computes a comprehensive set of lensing quantities from the deflection angles of a mass distribution.
  - Contents: JAX, Units, Data Structures, Grids, Mass Profile and Galaxy, Tracer, LensCalc, The Lens Equation, Deflection Angles, Hessian, Convergence, Shear, Magnification, Magnification At A Point, Critical Curves and Caustics, Einstein Radius, Fermat Potential, Wrap Up
- [Mappings](scripts/guides/mappings.py): A strong lens shows you the same source more than once. The science question that follows is always the same: **which part of the source is this piece of the image?**
  - Contents: Dataset, Mask, Point Mappings, Region Mappings, Parametric Source, Solver Refinement Steps, Magnification, Parametric Source, Region Mappings, Pixelized Source, Subplot Mappings, Brightest Image-Plane Positions for Spectroscopic Follow-Up (4MOST), Magnification per Image, Wrap Up
- [Guide: Witt-Wynne (SIEP) Projection and the isit4or2or1 Solver](scripts/guides/misc/witt_wynne.py): The singular isothermal elliptical *potential* (SIEP) is the one strong-lens model whose lens equation reduces to a quartic with a closed-form solution. Given a source position it returns, in microseconds and without any iteration, the number of images (4 / 3 / 2 / 1 -- 3 only for flattened lenses, ``e`` >~ 0.36, when the source crosses the pseudo-caustic), their positions, their signed magnifications and their time lags. That speed is what makes it usable inside a transient broker: when a supernova alert lands near a known quad, the question "is this a fourth image or a foreground star?" has to be answered before the object fades.
- [Modeling: Expectation Propagation](scripts/guides/modeling/advanced/expectation_propagation.py): In the `hierarchical` example, we fitted graphical models to a dataset comprising 3 images of strong lenses, which had a hierarchical parameter, the power-law `slope`. This provides the basis of composing and fitting complex graphical models to large datasets.
  - Contents: Sample Simulation, Dataset & Mask, Model Individual Factors, Analysis, Model, Paths, Analysis Factors, Factor Graph, Expectation Propagation, Cyclic Fitting, Result, Output, Results
- [Modeling: Graphical](scripts/guides/modeling/advanced/graphical.py): The example scripts throughout the workspace have focused on modeling **individual strong lens datasets**. From each fit, you may have inspected lens properties (e.g., Einstein radius) and source properties (e.g., magnification). You may even have analyzed many lenses one-by-one and combined their results to study global trends in galaxy formation or cosmology.
  - Contents: Initialization, Point Solver, Model, Analysis, Analysis Factors, Factor Graph, Search, Result, Wrap Up
- [Modeling: Hierarchical](scripts/guides/modeling/advanced/hierarchical.py): A hierarchical model assumes that certain model parameters are drawn from a **shared parent distribution** (e.g. a Gaussian). When we fit such a model, the parameters of this parent distribution (such as its `mean` and `sigma`) become explicit free parameters in the inference. Scientifically, these parent-distribution parameters are often of greatest interest because they describe **population-level trends**, rather than the properties of individual lenses.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Analysis, Model Individual Factors, Analysis Factors, Model, Factor Graph, Search, Result, Concept, Wrap Up
- [Modeling: Parallel Bug Fix](scripts/guides/modeling/bug_fix.py): Depending on the operating system (e.g. Linux, Mac, Windows) and Python version, running a Python script or Jupyter notebook may lead to a error being raised when the search begins.
  - Contents: The Fix, Trouble Shooting
- [Modeling: Chaining](scripts/guides/modeling/chaining.py): Non-linear search chaining is an advanced model-fitting approach which breaks the model-fitting procedure down into multiple non-linear searches, using the results of the initial searches to initialization parameter sampling in subsequent searches. This contrasts the `modeling` examples which each compose and fit a single lens model-fit using one non-linear search.
  - Contents: Concise Model Composition API, This Example, Dataset + Masking, Paths, Model (Search 1), Search + Analysis + Model-Fit (Search 1), Result (Search 1), Model Chaining, Model Centred Chaining, Search + Analysis + Model-Fit (Search 2), Result (Search 2), How is Search Chaining Used?, Detailed Explanation Of Prior Passing, EXAMPLE

- [Point Solver: Limitations and Assumptions](scripts/guides/point_solver/limitations.py): ``PointSolver`` finds the multiple images of a point source by tiling the image plane with triangles, tracing them to the source plane, and repeatedly halving the triangles that contain the source. It is fast and works inside ``jax.jit``, but it is a numerical search, so it has limits.
  - Contents: The Oracle, Using The PointSolver, Assumptions, Limitations, Wrap Up
- [Guide: Point-Source Pairing, Over-Prediction and Under-Prediction](scripts/guides/point_solver/pairing.py): When fitting multiple-image positions — the bread and butter of group- and cluster-scale lens modeling — the model tracer will not, in general, predict exactly the images you observed. A wrong (or merely uncertain) mass model predicts *extra* images that were never detected, or fails to produce an observed image at all. What the likelihood does in those two situations decides which models a sampler rewards, and historically lensing codes have handled it with quiet conventions rather than explicit choices.
- [Light Profiles](scripts/guides/profiles/light.py): This guide is the single-page tour of every light profile available in **PyAutoLens** (all of which are re-exported from **PyAutoGalaxy**): how to construct each one, how to evaluate its image on a grid, how to compose it into a model, and how to pull an instance back out of that model.
  - Contents: Overview & Docs URL, All Light Profiles (Survey), Detailed Example: Sersic Image, Linear Light Profiles, Operated Light Profiles, Basis, Light Profile in a Model, Model Instance from Light Profile, Multipole Light Profiles, Remaining Profiles Walkthrough
- [Light-and-Mass Profiles](scripts/guides/profiles/light_and_mass_profiles.py): This guide is the third and final entry in the `scripts/guides/profiles/` trilogy.  It covers the *stellar*, *dark-matter*, and *combined light-and-mass* profiles — the ones used to decompose a lens galaxy into its constituent matter components rather than to model the total mass with a single parametric profile.
  - Contents: Overview & Docs URL, All Profiles (Survey), Stellar Mass Detailed Example, Dark Mass Detailed Example, NFW Variants, Combined Light + Mass Profiles (`al.lmp`), Linear Combined Light + Mass (`al.lmp_linear`), Composing a Decomposed Bulge+Halo Model, Model Instance from Decomposed Model, Remaining Profiles Walkthrough, Back-References
- [Mass Profiles](scripts/guides/profiles/mass.py): This guide is the single-page tour of every lensing mass profile available in **PyAutoLens** (re-exported from **PyAutoGalaxy**): how to construct each one, how to evaluate its convergence and deflections on a grid, how to compose it into a model, and how to pull an instance back out of that model.
  - Contents: Overview & Docs URL, All Mass Profiles (Survey), Detailed Example: Isothermal, Mass Sheets, Point Mass, Mass Profile in a Model, Model Instance from Mass Profile, Multipole Mass Profile, Remaining Profiles Walkthrough, Follow-Up

- [Results: Latent Variables](scripts/guides/results/latent_variables.py): PyAutoLens ships a curated catalogue of lensing-specific latent variables — quantities derived from the lens model that aren't sampled directly but are computed from each posterior draw to give you Bayesian uncertainties on the science quantities you actually care about. This tutorial shows the catalogue, how to toggle individual latents via the workspace config, how to load latent results from a completed fit, and how to extend ``al.AnalysisImaging`` with your own derived quantities.
  - Contents: Lensing Latents in PyAutoLens: The eight library-shipped latents and what each one means physically., Toggling Latents: The workspace ``config/latent.yaml`` override., Model Fit: Reuse the shared quick fit (``_quick_fit.py``) that produces real latent output., Loading Latent Results: ``analysis.compute_latent_samples`` over a subset of PDF draws, and the two, Extending with a Custom Latent: Subclass ``al.AnalysisImaging`` to add lens-mass derived quantities., Contributing Upstream: When your custom latent is general enough, promote it to the library.
- [Results: Start Here](scripts/guides/results/start_here.py): After a lens model-fit completes, nearly everything a user could need is written to the `output/` folder. Most of it can be loaded back into full Python objects with a single line of code, via either `.json` files (for model objects like the `Tracer`, `Model` and samples) or `.fits` files (for imaging products like the model image, residuals and source-plane images).
  - Contents: Model Fit, Info

- [Flux](scripts/guides/units/flux.py): Absolute flux calibration in Astronomy is the process of converting the number of photons detected by a telescope into a physical unit of luminosity or a magnitude. For example, a luminosity might be given in units of solar luminosities or the brightness of a galaxy quoted as a magnitude in units of AB magnitudes.
  - Contents: Zero Point, Total Flux, Latent Variables
- [Author: Kaihao Wang](scripts/guides/units/mass_to_light_ratio_units.py): This guide is in development and not written with extensive text and descrptions (yet!).
- [Using JAX](scripts/guides/using_jax.py): **PyAutoLens** runs on either **NumPy** (the default) or **JAX** (Google's array library with GPU support and just-in-time compilation). JAX makes lens modeling 10-100x faster on large grids — sometimes more on GPU — so the library is built to use it automatically wherever it helps.
  - Contents: Auto-Enabled Modeling, Disabling JAX, Writing @jax.jit Yourself, Custom Likelihood Functions, JIT-ing Library Methods, Pytree Registration, The Pairing Rule, Grids Stay Outside the Boundary, Bound Methods and the JIT Cache, Return-Type Contract
